subject: Wonder request layout and prompt-cache behaviour of the mission service
cache_rules_source: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/prompt-caching (automatic prefix match from the first token; stable content first; prompt_cache_key routes requests together; prompt_cache_retention in_memory or 24h)

request_layout.instructions_chars: 49,196 to 56,077 = 23,187 static prompt + about 31,600 live context JSON rebuilt every turn (map.places alone 18,545 chars)
request_layout.cached_tokens_when_a_hit_occurred: 11,892 to 12,660 (exactly the unchanged prefix before the live context)
request_layout.follow_up_requests_with_any_cache_hit: 251 of 796; median gap to the previous request 9 s on hits and 12 s on misses
request_layout.evidence_images: 4K JPEG as base64 data URL, 12.6 to 13.1 MB each; request bodies up to 38.8 MB with three frames

input_token_attribution_estimate.method: least squares over 834 requests: input_tokens = text_chars / 2.8 + 1601 * images + 118 * reasoning_items (R2 0.98, median error 2,248 tokens)

change.instructions: static brief plus compact public map only, identical on every turn
change.live_context: newest input item labelled 'Current mission context (live system state, not an operator message)', never stored in the transcript
change.prompt_cache_key: mission id (bench_tools and accept_chat use their run names)
change.effort: operator picker in the composer (low, medium, high; each mission starts at high) via the set_effort message
change.wake_payloads: vehicles reduced to compact_vehicle; live telemetry arrives in the context item

proof_run.history: one operator line plus the live context item; the second request changes only a note inside the context item
